result.title: When Recognition Meets Discovery: Learning Need Not Be Entangled in One Representation Space
result.summary: Generalized Category Discovery (GCD) aims to recognize known classes while discovering novel categories from unlabeled data containing both old and novel samples. Existing methods typically optimize recognition and discovery within a shared representation space, implicitly assuming that the same representation geometry can serve both objectives. Through controlled spectral analysis, we uncover a striking asymmetry: old-class discrimination is increasingly concentrated in the dominant singular directions, while novel-class structure is better preserved in the complementary residual space. More importantly, strengthening the former can even degrade the latter, revealing that recognition and discovery compete for representation capacity rather than merely for optimization weight. Motivated by this observation, we propose Dual-Space Spectral Routing, which dynamically decomposes the representation via online SVD and routes supervised recognition and unsupervised discovery to complementary discriminative and general subspaces. We further exploit their distinct responses to old and novel samples to construct a dual-space novelty signal, which guides Subspace Relation Aggregation (SRA) for organizing candidate novel categories. Extensive experiments across multiple GCD baselines, backbones, and benchmarks demonstrate a consistently improved recognition-discovery balance without introducing additional inference parameters. Code will be open source.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究广义类别发现中已知类识别与新类发现之间的表征冲突，通过谱分析提出双空间谱路由，将监督识别与无监督发现分配到互补子空间，并利用双空间新类信号组织候选类别。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「识别与发现争夺表征容量」及主导／残差子空间分解，可能为诊断 LVR 内部状态中任务必要视觉信息与通用信息的分布提供启发，但方法面向图像类别发现，需核查向多模态推理状态迁移的可行性。
